tour.name: Phang Nga Bay Private Boat Tour from Phuket: James Bond Island, Sea Caves & Koh Panyee
tour.subtitle: A private day among the limestone towers of Phang Nga Bay with your own long-tail boat and guide: canoeing through sea caves into hidden lagoons, the needle rock of James Bond Island, lunch in the stilt village of Koh Panyee, the mangroves and a swim from a quiet beach.

tour.overview:
North-east of Phuket, Phang Nga Bay is a drowned landscape of more than forty limestone islands rising sheer from shallow green water, edged with mangroves and riddled with caves. Some islands are hollow, with collapsed caves forming hidden lagoons, called hongs, reached only at the right tide through low sea tunnels. The bay became famous when The Man with the Golden Gun was filmed at Khao Phing Kan in 1974, and much of it is protected as Ao Phang Nga National Park.

This private day explores the bay on your own long-tail boat with a guide, avoiding the crowded speedboat circuits. You paddle through sea caves into hongs, see James Bond Island at a quieter time, have lunch in the stilt village of Koh Panyee and finish with a swim.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 9 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Phuket
• Type: private car transfer, private long-tail boat with guide, canoes with paddlers
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy; canoes are paddled by local guides

WHAT YOU SEE
• The mangroves of the Phang Nga estuary.
• The sea caves and hongs of Koh Panak and Koh Hong.
• Khao Phing Kan and Ko Tapu (James Bond Island).
• Koh Panyee fishing village.
• A beach for swimming.

WHY THIS WORKS
We leave from a quieter pier on the Phang Nga side and time the visit to James Bond Island against the big groups, with canoe trips matched to the tide.

WHO IT SUITS
Couples, families and nature lovers.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you prefer white beaches and snorkelling, ask us for a private day to the Phi Phi islands.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
National park fees are charged per person. Sea conditions are calmer from November to April; in the monsoon some routes change.

days.name: Mangroves, sea caves and hongs, James Bond Island, lunch in Koh Panyee and a swim
days.description:
What to expect: the limestone islands of Phang Nga Bay from your own long-tail boat, with a guide, canoeing, park fees and lunch.

Your driver collects you at your hotel at about 8:00 and drives you over the Sarasin bridge to a pier on the Phang Nga side, about an hour. Your private long-tail boat heads out through channels lined with mangroves, where you may see monkeys, monitor lizards and kingfishers, into the open bay, where karst towers rise on every side.

At Koh Panak and Koh Hong, you transfer to inflatable canoes paddled by local guides, who take you through low sea caves – sometimes you lie back to pass under the rock – into the hongs, hidden lagoons open to the sky and surrounded by cliffs hung with plants, silent except for birds. You then reach Khao Phing Kan, two leaning limestone hills, and look out at Ko Tapu, the 20-metre needle of rock that stands in the water, made famous by the James Bond film. We aim for the quieter times between the waves of speedboats.

Lunch is at Koh Panyee, a village of some 2,000 people built on stilts in the shadow of a limestone cliff, founded by Muslim fishing families from Java two centuries ago. You eat fresh seafood on a terrace over the water and walk through its alleys, past the mosque and the famous floating football pitch built by the village children. In the afternoon the boat takes you to a quiet beach for a swim before returning to the pier, and your driver takes you back to your hotel at about 17:00.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
08:00 – Pick-up at your hotel in Phuket.
09:00 – Departure by long-tail boat through the mangroves.
10:00 – Sea canoeing at Koh Panak and Koh Hong.
11:30 – Khao Phing Kan and James Bond Island.
12:30 – Lunch in Koh Panyee.
14:00 – Swim at a quiet beach.
15:30 – Return to the pier.
17:00 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• The order changes with the tide, which decides when the cave entrances are passable.
• A sunset or overnight stay in the bay can be arranged.
• Bring dry bags for phones and cameras.

INCLUDED: private transfers, private long-tail boat and guide, canoeing, national park fees, lunch, fruit and drinks, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: alcoholic drinks, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Why a long-tail boat rather than a speedboat?
faq.answer: A private long-tail is quieter, more comfortable on the calm bay, and lets you go at your own pace instead of following the speedboat circuit.

faq.question: Do we have to paddle the canoes?
faq.answer: No. Local guides paddle and steer the canoes through the caves; you can try paddling in the lagoons if you like.

faq.question: Are the park fees included?
faq.answer: Yes, the national park fees, along with lunch, fruit and soft drinks.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children love the caves, the monkeys and the stilt village. Life jackets in children's sizes are provided.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Partly. Boarding the long-tail and canoes needs some agility; the bay can be enjoyed from the boat.

faq.question: Can non-swimmers join?
faq.answer: Yes. Life jackets are worn in the canoes, and swimming is optional.

faq.question: Is it suitable in the rainy season?
faq.answer: Phang Nga Bay is sheltered and often calm even from May to October, but trips can be changed or cancelled for safety in storms.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, fresh seafood in Koh Panyee; vegetarian options are available. The village is Muslim, so no alcohol is served there.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tips are appreciated in Thailand but never required.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Swimwear, quick-dry clothes, sandals, a hat, sun cream and a dry bag for electronics.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: November to April for calm seas and sunshine. The bay is beautiful all year, but rain is more frequent from May to October.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 48 hours before the tour, and at no cost if the trip is cancelled for weather. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
